explanation: Ada Lovelace, daughter of the poet Lord Byron, saw that such a machine could work with symbols as well as numbers. The engine itself was never completed.

claims.text: In 1843 Ada Lovelace published notes that included a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.
Mary Somerville, Grace Hopper and Florence Nightingale did not write these 1843 notes.
Ada Lovelace was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron.
Lovelace wrote that the Analytical Engine could act on things other than numbers, such as musical notes.
Babbage's Analytical Engine was never completed.
